questions.question: Explain the meaning of change and continuity, with an example of each from the East Coast trade.
questions.expected_answer: Change means something became different over time; for example, the centre of trade moved from Mapungubwe to Great Zimbabwe after about 1300. Continuity means something stayed the same; for example, gold and ivory were traded out and glass beads and cloth came in for hundreds of years.

questions.question: List three continuities in the East Coast trade from about 900 to 1500 AD.
questions.expected_answer: Gold and ivory went out and glass beads and cloth came in. Goods were carried inland on foot by porters and across the sea in dhows using the monsoon winds. Swahili merchants at coastal towns such as Sofala and Kilwa were middlemen. Inland leaders who controlled trade became rich and powerful. Most people remained farmers and herders.

questions.question: Describe three changes in the East Coast trade over this time.
questions.expected_answer: The centre of power moved from Schroda to K2, to Mapungubwe and then to Great Zimbabwe after about 1300. Kilwa grew very rich by controlling much of the gold trade through Sofala. Around 1500, the Portuguese arrived, attacked some coastal towns and built a fort at Sofala in 1505 to try to control the gold trade.
